transcript.text: Hi, my Bosch WAN28281GB has stopped half way through a wash and is showing E18. Water still in the drum. What does that mean?

E18 means the washer has not drained, or has taken too long to drain. With water still in the drum, the usual cause is a blocked pump filter/coin trap; less commonly it is a kink or blockage in the drain hose or household waste pipe, or a failed drain pump. Switch it off and unplug it first. Put towels and a shallow tray under the lower-front filter flap, then loosen the filter slowly—water may come out. Remove any coins, lint or small items, and check the filter is clean. If accessible, gently feel whether the small pump impeller behind it is jammed; do not force it. Refit the filter securely before trying a drain or spin programme. If the filter is clear or it still will not drain afterwards, the hose/waste connection or pump needs narrowing down.
Thanks, I'll give that a go. I've unplugged it. Should I empty the water out first before undoing the filter? There's quite a lot in the drum. No burning smell or anything like that.

Yes—if there is a small emergency-drain hose behind the lower-front flap, use that first. With the machine still unplugged, put towels down and drain it into a shallow tray or bowl in small stages; refit its cap between trips to empty the container. If there is no little hose, you can still loosen the filter very slowly, only a little at a time, letting water out into the tray and tightening it again as needed—do not fully remove it while the drum is full. Once most of the water is out, remove the filter and clear any debris. E18 is a drainage-timeout code, most often a blocked filter/impeller, but a restricted drain hose or waste pipe can give the same result.

Right, I've drained it using the little hose behind the flap. It took several trays and towels and the water was grey and smelled a bit. Floor got a little wet but nothing near the socket. I'll undo the filter now.

That is the right next step. Keep towels and the tray in place, as a little more water may still come out; with the machine unplugged, remove the filter fully and clear out any lint, coins, hair grips or small fabric items. Then use a torch to look into the opening and gently turn the small plastic impeller with a finger—do not force it. It should move with some slight magnetic resistance but must not be solidly jammed, and the vanes should not be broken. Tell me what you find in the filter and whether the impeller is free, jammed, or damaged; that will separate a simple blockage from a hose restriction or likely pump fault.
Found a child's sock and a hair grip wrapped round the filter, plus a lot of fluff. The impeller turns, slightly notchy at first and then free. What should I do next?

That sock, hair grip and fluff are a very convincing cause of the E18, and the slight notchiness is normal magnetic resistance if the impeller then turns freely. Clean the filter seal and its seating surface, then screw the filter back in straight and fully hand-tight. With towels still nearby, plug the machine back in and run a drain or spin-only programme; stay with it for the first minute and check around the filter flap for any drips. If it drains normally, the blockage was the fault. If the pump hums but no water leaves, the next likely restriction is the drain hose or household waste connection; if it is completely silent, the drain pump or its electrical supply needs an engineer.
Thanks, I've cleaned it, refitted the filter and plugged it back in. I've run a rinse and spin programme and it drained quickly, E18 has gone and it spins normally. No drips from the flap either.

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. That has fixed it: the sock, hair grip and fluff had blocked the pump filter and caused the E18 drain timeout. As a precaution, check trouser pockets and small children’s items before washing, and clean the pump filter periodically—especially if you notice slower draining. Is there anything else you’d like help with?
